title: How to Send a Video as a GIF on WhatsApp from iPhone
description: WhatsApp turns videos of 6 seconds or less into GIFs. How to use the built-in GIF switch on iPhone, and what to do for longer clips or more control over it.
h1: How to send a video as a GIF on WhatsApp from iPhone
card_title: Send a video as a GIF on WhatsApp
card_summary: The built-in 6-second GIF switch, and the way around its limits.
quick_answer: In a WhatsApp chat tap +, choose Photo & Video Library and pick a video. Trim it to 6 seconds or less and a GIF switch appears next to the camera icon above the trim bar; tap GIF, then Send. For clips you want to crop, slow down via frame rate, loop a set number of times or reuse in other apps, make the GIF in Make Video to GIF first and share the file to WhatsApp.
intro: WhatsApp has had a video-to-GIF switch on iPhone for years, but it hides it until the clip is short enough: six seconds or less.
That covers most reactions. When you need something it can't do, such as a tighter crop, a specific frame rate or a GIF you can also post on Discord or Slack, convert the clip first.

sections.heading: WhatsApp's built-in GIF switch
list: Open the chat, tap + and choose Photo & Video Library.
Drag the ends of the timeline at the top until the clip is 6 seconds or shorter.
Tap GIF next to the camera icon; the clip starts looping.
Optionally add text, emoji or a drawing, then tap Send.
sections.note: If you don't see the GIF option, the selection is still longer than 6 seconds.

sections.heading: When to make the GIF first
paragraphs: Make the GIF in Make Video to GIF when you want to crop to a face or an object, choose the frame rate, set a loop count, or keep the same GIF to post elsewhere. Export it, tap Share and pick WhatsApp; the chat receives the animation.

steps.heading: Step by step: GIF first, then WhatsApp
steps.intro: For clips that need more than WhatsApp's switch.

items.name: Open the video
items.text: Pick the clip in Make Video to GIF.

items.name: Trim and crop
items.text: Keep the best seconds and crop to the subject.

items.name: Set FPS and loop
items.text: 12–15 FPS and an infinite loop suit chat reactions.

items.name: Share to WhatsApp
items.text: Tap Share, choose WhatsApp and pick the chat.

tips.heading: Tips
items: Keep chat GIFs small: people often open them on mobile data.
A crop around a face makes reactions readable in a small chat bubble.
WhatsApp's own GIF search (the GIF tab in the sticker panel) is quicker for stock reactions.

faq.question: Why can't I send a video as a GIF on WhatsApp?
faq.answer: The GIF option only appears when the trimmed clip is 6 seconds or shorter. Shorten the selection and it shows up.

faq.question: Can a WhatsApp GIF be longer than 6 seconds?
faq.answer: Not with the built-in switch. Make the GIF in another app first, then share it to WhatsApp, and keep the file small.

faq.question: Will the other person see it move?
faq.answer: Yes. WhatsApp plays GIFs on iPhone and Android as looping animations.
